To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the optimal path for a hypersonic lifting-body entry into a nonuniform atmosphere consists of extremal lift subarc(s) and singular subarc(s), and that the optimal lift on the singular arc is always dominated by that due to the atmospheric density variation, and is bounded.

(1) the optimal path consists, in general, of two kinds of arcs, namely, extremal lift arcs and singular arcs, (2) the singular arc is always dominated by atmospheric density, (3) the singular arc may be admissible only below a certain altitude, and (4) the number of sub-arcs, their sequence and the location of the switching points depend on the initial re-entry conditions.

the optimal path for the hypersonic lifting body is a sequence of extremal lift subarc, followed by a singular subarc, followed again by an extremal lift sub arc, and so on, with the singular subarc becoming inadmissible above certain altitude.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a general methodology for solving the optimal re-entry problem.
the problem of optimal control of a hypersonicleaning body during planetary entry.
the problem of determining the optimal lift control of an entry body during planetary re-entry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optimal lift control problem is solved completely for all cases considered.

the lift control problem of the present investigation can be solved analytically for the case where the variation of the aerodynamic coefficient of the vehicle is negligible, and the lift control problem for a constant atmospheric density can be solved analyitically for a more general case.

the optimal lift control of the lifting body during entry is a two-phase process, i.e., the lift control during the first phase is governed by the variation of the atmosphere density and the lift control during second phase is governed by an optimal re-entry angle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the optimal path is composed of a single extremal lift arc followed by a singular lift arc.
a hypersonic lifting entry is a three-dimensional problem, i.e., it involves three state variables, three control variables, three switching points, and three subarcs.
the optimal lift control problem for a hypersonic lifting entry vehicle can be completely solved in closed form if the atmospheric density is constant or if it varies according to an exponential law.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimal path is not a simple bang-bang lift trajectory as in the case of constant atmospheric density.
the singular subarcs are not necessarily inadmissible and that the number of subarc switches can vary with the initial conditions.
, in general, the number of switching points is not uniquely determined and can be any positive integer.
